واژگان و اصطلاحات جدید را در زمینه و بافت جمله یادداشت کنید تا در حافظه بلندمدت تثبیت شوند.
پس از پایان هر فصل، نکات کلیدی و آموخته‌های خود را مرور کرده و به زبان خود خلاصه کنید.

content: 32 december 3 :: vol 29 no 14 :: 2014 NURSING STANDARD Key Excellent ★★★★★ Very good ★★★★ Good ★★★ Average ★★ Poor ★ MyNHS Health secretary Jeremy Hunt launched the MyNHS website, part of the NHS Choices portal, on November 19, announcing that it will shine a light on performance, allow patients to compare care and help spread best practice. It features consultant outcome data for a range of specialties, allowing the performance of 5,000 surgeons in England to be rated and compared. The information shows how many times a consultant has performed a particular procedure. Other quality measures are being added, notably length of hospital stay, the rates of readmission and complications, adverse events and mortality rates. As the site develops, it will oﬀ er statistics on local hospital performance, mental health care, social care and public health. There is quality indicator information on hospitals, with Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspection ratings, A&E performance, staﬀ recommendations, levels of infection control and cleanliness, the number of patients waiting more than 52 weeks for treatment, as well as the percentage of patients who recommend the hospital. From early December, the CQC’s individual risk rating for GP practices will be included, with more data to be added next year, including one-year and ﬁ ve-year cancer survival rates for NHS trusts in England. www.nhs.uk/mynhs See www.nursing-standard.co.uk for previous website reviews WEBWISE Reviews TV :: radio :: books :: websites :: apps Research Methods in Health: Investigating Health and Health Services – Fourth edition ★★★★★ This bestselling book has an established place in the literature on health and health services research. It covers a wide range of topics, from health economics to grounded theory. The claim made in its title to provide guidance on issues raised by the requirement to evaluate health services in their totality is borne out by sections such as the one on health needs assessment. It offers detailed discussion of the theoretical assumptions that underpin each facet of the research process. Many competing texts provide practical guidance on how to carry out particular research methods, but coverage of the philosophical implications that such actions imply is often sparse. It sometimes seems that approaches to research in nursing are strongly inﬂ uenced by current trends in the wider world of social research. Ann Bowling’s chapter on focus groups provides a sound foundation for nurses interested in using them in their research. The popularity of mixed methods approaches is also reﬂ ected in an extensive chapter. The Body Keeps the Score – Mind, Brain and Body in the Transformation of Trauma ★★★★★ This exceptional book helps us understand the complexities of traumatic experiences. Psychiatrist Bessel van der Kolk argues that while humans are a resilient species and able to rebound from wars, violence and disasters, trauma leaves traces on our minds, our emotions, our metabolism, physiology and immune systems. Founder and medical director of the Trauma Centre in Boston, Massachusetts, Dr van der Kolk has researched post-traumatic stress since the 1970s. His work has resulted in the development of the diagnosis of developmental trauma disorder and the beneﬁ ts of yoga, theatre, neurofeedback and eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing therapy for traumatic stress. Excess stress predisposes us to diabetes, heart disease and cancer. It is, he argues, one of the West’s most urgent public health issues. Throughout the book, he draws on a wide range of fascinating case studies to back up his claim that ‘the body keeps the score’. Dr van der Kolk looks at lessons from Vietnam veterans, the minds of children, abusive relationships and neglect, traumatic memory and ‘the unbearable heaviness of remembering’. This is an intense, thought-provoking read written for the general reader. I recommend it unreservedly. It is a book I will keep and treasure and, I am sure, return to time and again.
